newsitem.title: UK: Celltech bounces on reassuring press comment.
newsitem.headline: Celltech bounces on reassuring press comment.

text.p: Shares in biotech group Celltech Plc rose on Thursday, rebounding from its slump on Wednesday after development work on a drug for treating sceptic shock was dropped.

The Financial Times Lex column noted that other biotech stocks had rebounded after setbacks on leading products. It said Celltech had a promising development pipeline and still had 41 million stg in the bank.
With bargain-hunters moving in after the stock halved in value on Wednesday, Celltech shares were up 16-1/2p at 357-1/2 by 0755 GMT in volume of 150,097 shares.
However analysts at Lehman Brothers said Celltech was "not a buying opportunity" despite Wednesday's tumble.
"We expect the stock to be a lacklustre performer near-term, in the absence of important new information," said Lehman analyst Ian Smith in a research note.

"This could include a new collaboration with a major partner for other indications for the drug, but we do not expect this in the near term. We do not now expect the company to be profitable until 2001 (previously break-even projected for 1998/99)."

Smith repeated a "venture" rating on Celltech shares, with a 12-month price target of 515p, assuming other key drugs continue to progress satisfactorily. -- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4367
